q7.answer: Each pod polls the config service's routing record every 10 seconds (with jitter). When the revision changes and names a new active version, the pod switches to it from its warm set, or downloads it from the artifact store and checks the digest first. No redeploy is involved, and the pointer change takes effect within one poll interval.

q8.answer: The shadow model takes the same feature row the user's response used, which is copied into the shadow event after the response body is written. On the request path, enqueueing is bounded to 1 ms and drops the event if the queue is full or the enqueue is slow, so it never waits or retries. Shadow inference runs on a separate fleet with its own CPU and memory, so it cannot add to the request's latency.

q9.answer: The shadow queue is bounded, and dropping events is allowed: when it is full, request-side enqueues are dropped and counted. Workers discard events whose queue lag exceeds 60 seconds and count them. If batch writes keep failing, the fleet stops consuming and the queue drops events. Lost events shrink the sample without biasing the rates, and no user sees any change. The queue size itself is not specified in the plan.

q10.answer: Each shadow event produces one row in the analytics store holding the active items, the candidate items or error, both latencies, the fallback flag, the candidate status and the schema version and as_of, so no join is needed. A daily job compares overlap@20, rank correlation, the share of candidate items outside the active top 20, catalog coverage, the fallback rates on the same denominator, and operational metrics. It writes one gate report per day against the candidate version in the registry.

q11.answer: A model may run for a user only if its feature_schema is in the store manifest and every required feature is present in that user's row. The check runs at registration, at promotion for every shadow day, at pod load, per request for the active model (which falls back with feature_contract_mismatch and raises an alert), and per event for the candidate (which records skipped_incompatible without running). The config service repeats the check at activation.

q12.answer: Rollback is one CAS config write that sets active_version to previous_active, sets previous_active to the removed version, and increments revision. Pods pick it up within one 10-second poll interval plus apply time, and the previous version needs no download because it stays in the warm set. This is a design estimate: the plan requires a staging drill and a real-fleet measurement against a 60-second target, and neither has been run yet. The previous version is rechecked against the current manifest, and if that check fails, the kill switch is used instead.
